- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 3–5 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- If sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and model shows rising trend, it’s likely overconfident — dampen forecast slope or add downward drift.
- In high-event periods (≥15 events/30d), model tends to overreact to auction supply — reduce forecast sensitivity to supply net unless bullish sentiment is strong.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 30d mean, check if sentiment or event context suggests mean reversion — apply correction toward historical mean if no strong directional signal.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to capture volatility — use moving average of sentiment to adjust forecast volatility.
